newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks close down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks close down on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed lower Monday as dealers took profits on cue from a sliding Dow Jones.

"Dealers took profits on some stocks. The bourse is taking a breather before another rally. The short-term outlook is still good," said Roberto Galvan, an equity analyst at the Bursametrica consultancy. "Razor-thin volume also lent itself to same-day buy-sell trades," he added.
The blue chip IPC index closed off 30.60 points, or 0.91 percent, at 3,345.45. Volume was lifeless at 29.3 million shares traded.

Technical analysts stressed that while the IPC did fall, they saw its failure to hit the 3,300-point mark as a positive sign, and put it down to expectations that primary interest rates would fall at Tuesday's auction.
Bank stock Intenal headed the percentage gainers' list, up 46 centavos (6 cents) to 7.60 pesos ($1.01), but after just 11,000 shares were traded.
On the broad market, a total of 102 stocks changed hands, of which losers outnumbered winners by 55 to 21, with the remaining 26 unchanged.
